observations: Viewed baseline and candidate face crops and complete stages for each of three accepted views: 12 actual PNGs.

Adult unobstructed head: the lower-screen brow loses ragged dark fragments through its middle and reads as a smoother continuous arch. The upper-screen brow retains slight stippling at this pixel size. The improvement is visible in the face crop and modest in the full stage.

Adult support: the exposed brow beside the upper-screen fingertips has a cleaner continuous edge. The lower-screen brow is very small and looks largely unchanged at stage size. Supporting fingers, palm, wrist, head silhouette and other facial features remain visually consistent.

Infant high contrast: the brow difference is barely perceptible at this narrow viewport. The closed-eye expression, white face, nose contour, hand placement and framing remain legible and visually consistent.

No visible new gaps, floating facial details, unintended face-color changes, or other regressions appeared in these comparisons. All three native summaries record the frozen candidate hash, unchanged inputs and one successful workflow.
limitations: The brow improvement is localized and subtle at full stage size; the upper-screen adult brow still shows some fine stippling.
Review covers three fixed raw-module browser views only, not every age, camera angle, animation frame or pose.
This visual review does not test the full application loader, deployment or clinical correctness.
